label: SECONDARY DIAGNOSTIC -- NOT PRIMARY RESULT. Official Loghi result (beam width 10) is unchanged.
hypothesis_preregistered: If Loghi's corpus-wide under-production (deletion-heavy edits, median prediction/reference length ratio 0.86) and its 71 empty outputs are a beam-search-width artifact, a narrower beam (greedy, beam=1) should make both worse or unchanged, and there is no supported profile above beam=10 to test the opposite direction with the current model_registry.py. This tests only whether beam width in the range actually used (1 vs 10) explains any material part of the gap.
conclusion: Beam width 10 is already marginally better than greedy on every measure (lower CER/WER, fewer empty outputs, fewer deletions) -- confirming beam 10 as the right primary choice, not something to change. But the effect size is tiny (0.30 percentage points of CER) against a 14.3-point gap to Lion, and the empty-output count only drops from 91 to 71, not to zero. Beam width does not materially explain the gap or the empty-output phenomenon; both persist essentially unchanged across the only two supported profiles. This is evidence AGAINST a decoding-configuration explanation and points toward a cause upstream of decoding (preprocessing/architecture/training), not the search width.
